result:
I found 12 rules whose code didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. I wrote a reference implementation from the docstrings and compared it with all 150 rules over a grid of inputs. Before the fixes there were 12 mismatches; after them, none.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 87, 138, 140 | The cap only kicked in once the discount exceeded twice the cap (`min(disc, cap) if disc > 2*cap else disc`), so discounts between the cap and twice the cap went through uncapped | Changed to plain `min(disc, cap)` |
| 16 | Used `round(... / 100)`, which can round up, against the module rule that discounts are floored to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 30 | Used `qty > 100`, so the discount didn't apply at exactly 100 units | Changed to `qty >= 100` |
| 118 | Threshold was 6 instead of 5 | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 135 | Threshold was 13 instead of 12 | Changed to `qty >= 12` |
| 45, 47, 134 | Capped the price before applying the percentage, against the module rule that the discount (not the price) is capped | Apply the percentage first, then `min(disc, cap)` |
| 86 | Docstring says "whole" but the code discounted only units above 50 (marginal) | Changed to `base * 2 // 100` |

Rules 83, 113, 142 and 147 write the cap as `if disc > cap: disc = cap` instead of `min()`. That gives the same result, so I left them as they are.

STATUS: DONE
